title: Verify two-factor authentication
purpose: Confirm a sign-in or sensitive account action with an enrolled factor.

sections.title: Page variants
paragraphs: The sign-in variant requires a pending MFA login stage for an account with an enabled primary factor. Without it, the page returns to sign-in. The reauthentication variant requires a signed-in account with an available enrolled code method and may be opened without a stored pending operation. These pages verify existing factors; they do not enroll or reset one.

items.label: Code
items.description: Required current six-digit authenticator code or unused eight-digit recovery code. Recovery codes are consumed on successful validation. TOTP uses the default 30-second step and refuses reuse of an already accepted current code. Invalid attempts are rate limited.

items.label: Sign In
items.description: Sign-in variant: validates the factor, records usage and completes the pending stage.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Sign-in variant only: posts sign-out, abandons the stage and returns to sign-in. The reauthentication form does not have this button.

items.label: Confirm
items.description: Reauthentication variant: records a recent factor check, then resumes the protected action or returns to the application destination.

items.label: Alternative options
items.description: Reauthentication variant: Use your password appears when a usable password is available. Security-key alternatives are not offered by the committed factor configuration.

sections.title: Limits
paragraphs: A successful code proves this account’s enrolled factor, not a laboratory qualification or role. The committed configuration does not offer trusted-browser skipping. Reauthentication is considered recent for five minutes; normal sign-in and sensitive-action policies remain distinct.

sections.title: Sign-in activity
paragraphs: In the sign-in variant, a rejected code records a failed sign-in in the deployment’s application logs. Completing all required sign-in stages records one successful sign-in. Logs name the stored username and never include the code. Canceling an unfinished sign-in does not record a sign-out for an authenticated session. These logs follow the deployment’s retention and survive database resets. The reauthentication variant does not create a new sign-in or sign-out event.
